nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 5$, some prime $p > 5$ divides one of $k$, $k+1$, $k+2$, $k+3$, $k+4$.
nodes.title: Five consecutive integers above five have a prime factor above five

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 4$, some prime $p > 4$ divides one of $k$, $k+1$, $k+2$, $k+3$.
nodes.title: Four consecutive integers above four have a prime factor above four

nodes.summary: Let $n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$ and $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$, assume $N \ge 6$, and for a natural number $m$ let $P(m)$ denote the product of all primes at most $m$. If $n! \cdot P(\lfloor N/3 \rfloor) \cdot \prod_{i=2}^{L} P(\lfloor N^{1/i} \rfloor) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Erdős layer criterion with a one-third first layer for a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$ and $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$, and for a natural number $m$ let $P(m)$ denote the product of all primes at most $m$. If $n! \cdot P(n) \cdot \prod_{i=2}^{L} P(\lfloor N^{1/i} \rfloor) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Erdős layer criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers. If $n! \cdot (k+n-1)^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Half-exponent criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers and let $\pi(n)$ be the number of primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot (k+n-1)^{\pi(n)} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Prime-counting criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$, and let $P(n)$ denote the product of all primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot N^{\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor + 1} \cdot P(n) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Square-root and primorial criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and $k > n$ be natural numbers with $n! \cdot 2^{n-1} < k$. Then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Large starts give a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 38$ and $k > n^2$ be natural numbers. Then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.
nodes.title: Quadratic starts give a large prime in a consecutive block

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 6$, some prime $p > 6$ divides one of $k$, $k+1$, $k+2$, $k+3$, $k+4$, $k+5$.
nodes.title: Six consecutive integers above six have a prime factor above six

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 3$, one of the three integers $k$, $k + 1$, $k + 2$ is divisible by a prime $p > 3$.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Schur theorem for three consecutive integers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 2$, one of the two integers $k$, $k + 1$ is divisible by a prime $p > 2$.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Schur theorem for two consecutive integers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
